scope: Synthetic one-layer, single-lane, closed-loop BF16 AFD FFN component study with changing request lengths and device-derived expert counts; not full-model serving or a DeepEP baseline comparison.

hardware.placement: two four-GPU NVLink domains, four FFN + four Attention
hardware.network: one explicitly selected common RoCE rail per domain; NCCL GPU-initiated RDMA

method.order: variant order rotated once per repeat; identical seeded request traces across variants
method.latency: per request maximum completed host-wall interval across four Attention ranks; p50/p95/p99 summarized as median of three per-trace quantiles
method.cuda_event: per-request maximum across four Attention ranks; includes GPU queue gaps and peer waiting, not CPU work before the start event
method.ffn_host_submission: per-request median across four FFN ranks; includes blocking host count read in dynamic_eager, so it is not pure launch API time
method.throughput: useful source tokens / maximum rank whole-trace wall; includes GPU input generation and source pre-request drain, excluded from individual request latency
method.capture: six pooled graphs captured and replay-primed before each timed trace; startup measured separately and excluded from request latency and trace throughput
method.memory: mean of four FFN per-rank peaks minus each rank pre-setup baseline; allocated and reserved baselines subtracted separately; resident weights baseline and native GIN transport allocations excluded
method.allocation: logical workspace and PyTorch caching-allocator requests/bytes differ from physical device allocation calls; graph FFN request/device-allocation deltas verified zero
method.cgroup: four local ranks share one pod cgroup; report rank0/rank4 representative deltas once per group plus within-group ranges; never sum rank copies
method.correctness: all three variants passed independent numerical checks and final live-output checks after each timed trace; pooled addresses stable
method.request_table_index: each timing row joins the same zero-based row in request_traces[trace_id].requests; request metadata shared across modes and variants

limitations: Closed-loop completion before buffer reuse; no cross-request overlap, concurrent lanes, scheduler or full-model TTFT.
Host source lengths are known; expert counts and routing are produced from GPU data.
The live path preserves fixed-capacity storage while device live counts limit payload; expert groups still retain alignment padding.
One workload shape and two-node topology; p99 and CPU scheduling can vary, so raw per-request values and shared-cgroup counters are retained.
Before/after implementation also changes worker loops and graph first-replay priming; its entire delta cannot be attributed causally to live counts alone.

final_live_profiling.configuration: FINAL live-token hybrid implementation; separate instrumented 300-request trace per variant, one repeat, eight ranks; profiling times are not latency benchmark results
final_live_profiling.aggregation: Per-process per-request metrics. Role summaries combine four ranks x 300 requests; no GPU times are summed across ranks.
final_live_profiling.gap_definition: Sum strictlypositive holes between merged GPU kernel intervals from first kernel start to last kernel end. A hole may include a device copy; it is not automatically CPU overhead.
cautions: API durations can overlap GPU work. Kernel durations include peer waits and GIN completion. Profile overhead invalidates direct comparison with unprofiled latency. Source staging copies are timed. Cross-node Nsight clocks are not aligned.
GIN kernel duration includes device-side completion and peer waiting; it is not pure wire-transfer time.
The roughly 75 ms reply-kernel outlier has no device-allocation or module-load API calls in that request; the underlying GIN/backend cause remains unresolved.
Initial and final profiles also differ in worker-loop behavior and graph first-replay priming; the whole change is not causally attributable to removing source padding.
